To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temporal focus of a narrative can be represented by the set of all event intervals, that the temporal focus is the set of all intervals in which the narrative has a temporal focus, and that the temporal focus has the property that the temporal focus does not contain any intervals in which the temporal focus is not contained.

(1) tense and aspect are assigned to event intervals and subintervals, (2) tense and aspect can change when there is a switch in reference points, (3) tense and aspect must be assigned to quoted and unquoted material, (4) modal events are assigned tense and aspect in the same way as other events, and (5) tense and aspect in narrative discourse are not assigned by rules that are specific to the narrative genre.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of generating a coherent and readable narrative from a formal encoding of a story.
a formalization of the temporal structure of discourse and with the assignment of tense and aspect for narrative discourse.
the problem of how to represent temporal information in a way that is both precise and readable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tense and aspect assignment in narrative discourse is not a simple matter, and that the problem has been approached from many different angles.
the tense/aspect assignment method described in the paper is useful in a number of ways.
the tense/aspect assignment is a complex task that is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system can assign tenses and aspects correctly 90.6% of the time, with a 1.4% error rate.
we have developed an algorithm that can be applied to any temporal encoding of events, and that it can be used to realize a variety of tense/aspect combinations.
we have designed a method for assigning temporal reference that is based on an explicit encoding of time and that is sensitive to discourse context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal structure of a discourse can be used to guide the selection of tenses and aspects.
tense and aspect are best viewed as a system that is sensitive to the temporal structure of events.
